ev.q: In 2016, among 78,360 persons who filled prescriptions for PrEP in the United States, women accounted for only 4.7%.
From 2014 to 2016, the annual number of PrEP users aged ≥16 years increased by 470%, from 13,748 to 78,360.
The annual number of PrEP users aged ≥16 years increased by 470%, from 13,748 in 2014 to 78,360 in 2016
Approximately 7% of the estimated 1.1 million persons who had indications for PrEP were prescribed PrEP in 2016
Women accounted for 3,678 (4.7%) of the 78,360 PrEP users
Males accounted for 95.3% of all PrEP users.
In 2016, 65.0% of PrEP users were aged 25–44 years
this study found that nearly six times as many white men and women were prescribed PrEP as were black men and women.

methods_quotes.q: CDC estimated the annual number of PrEP users based on a previously developed algorithm
persons prescribed TDF/FTC for ≤30 days were defined as postexposure prophylaxis users and excluded
the remaining persons with TDF/FTC prescribed for >30 days were considered PrEP users
PrEP use among persons prescribed TDF/FTC for >28 days was also estimated
Percentages calculated among 32,853 (41.9%) >30-day users and 39,654 (40.2%) >28-day users with information on race/ethnicity available.
